Tooltip_craft_saltingTubDesc: Presses up to 50 weight of salt-packed fish under a weighted board for 12 hours. Nothing more goes in until the pressed fish is taken out.
Tooltip_craft_dryingFrameDesc: Hangs up to 8 stacks of fish, up to 2.5 weight each, in the open air for 12 to 30 days. Salt Pressed fish dries fastest in warm, dry weather. Gutted fish needs a cold season, or it spoils. Rain stops the drying.
Tooltip_craft_dryingBeamMediumDesc: Hangs up to 4 stacks of fish, up to 15 weight each, on hooks. Dries like a Fish Drying Frame, for fish too big to hang on one. Outdoors only.
Tooltip_craft_dryingBeamLargeDesc: Hangs up to 2 stacks of fish, up to 50 weight each, on hooks. Dries like a Fish Drying Frame, for the biggest fish. Outdoors only.
Tooltip_craft_hangFishToDry: Salt drying, for Salt Pressed fish. Works in any season, fastest in warm, dry air. Keeps for months.
Tooltip_craft_hangFishToColdDry: Cold drying, for gutted fish and halves. Needs a cold season outdoors, or the fish rots. Keeps for a year or more.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Pack: Takes 2 salt for each started half weight of the packed fish, at least 2. Carry the salt yourself: a shaker holds 10, a Bag of Salt 50. A fish over 4.5 weight is too thick to salt whole: gut and split it first.
Press it in a Salting Tub before it spoils.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Pres: Cured, but not yet preserved. Hang it on a Fish Drying Frame.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Gutt: Hang it on a Fish Drying Frame in a cold season, or cook it. Split it if it's too heavy to hang.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Half: Hang it on a Fish Drying Frame in a cold season, or cook it.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Cold: Keeps for a year or more. Too hard to use: rehydrate it in water before cooking.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Drie: Keeps for months. Very salty: rehydrate it in water before cooking.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFish_Head: Raw, it will make you sick. Cook it, or add it to a soup or stew. It can't be dried. It also makes chum.
Fish head stock, ready to take up to 6 stew ingredients and your seasonings. It starts out as tasty as a plain stew. Cook it before eating.
